content: A small number of patients who have used pimecrolimus cream or similar medications have developed skin cancer or lymphoma, which is a type of cancer affecting the immune system. However, there is insufficient evidence to determine whether pimecrolimus cream directly caused these cancers. Research involving transplant patients, laboratory animals, and the mechanism of action of pimecrolimus suggests that there may be an increased risk of cancer for individuals using this medication. Further studies are required to better understand this potential risk. To minimize the risk of developing cancer while using pimecrolimus cream, follow these guidelines carefully: Use pimecrolimus cream only when you have symptoms of eczema. Discontinue use when your symptoms resolve or when your doctor advises you to stop. Avoid using the cream continuously for extended periods. Contact your doctor if you have been using pimecrolimus cream for six weeks and your eczema symptoms have not improved. You may need a different treatment. Inform your doctor if your eczema symptoms return after completing treatment with pimecrolimus cream. Apply pimecrolimus cream only to areas of skin affected by eczema. Use the smallest amount necessary to control your symptoms. Do not use pimecrolimus cream to treat eczema in children under two years of age. Notify your doctor if you have a history of cancer, particularly skin cancer, or any condition that affects your immune system. If you are unsure whether a condition you have impacts your immune system, consult your doctor. Pimecrolimus may not be suitable for you. Protect your skin from both natural and artificial sunlight during treatment. Avoid sunlamps, tanning beds, and ultraviolet light therapy. Minimize sun exposure even when the cream is not on your skin. If you must be outdoors, wear loose-fitting clothing to shield treated areas and consult your doctor about additional sun protection measures. Your doctor or pharmacist will provide you with a Medication Guide from the manufacturer when you begin treatment with pimecrolimus and each time you refill your prescription. Read this information carefully and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. You can also visit the FDA website or the manufacturer’s website for the Medication Guide. Discuss the risks of using pimecrolimus with your doctor. Pimecrolimus is prescribed to manage the symptoms of eczema (atopic dermatitis), a skin condition characterized by dryness, itching, and sometimes red, scaly rashes. It is used only for patients who cannot use other eczema medications or whose symptoms are not controlled by other treatments. Pimecrolimus belongs to a class of medications called topical calcineurin inhibitors, which work by suppressing the immune system’s production of substances that contribute to eczema. Pimecrolimus cream is applied to the skin, typically twice daily, for up to six weeks at a time. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Apply the cream exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it or apply it more frequently than prescribed. Pimecrolimus cream is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes or mouth. If the cream gets into your eyes, rinse them with cold water. If swallowed, contact your doctor immediately. To apply the cream: 1. Wash your hands with soap and water. 2. Ensure the affected skin is dry. 3. Apply a thin layer of pimecrolimus cream to all affected areas, including the head, face, and neck if necessary. 4. Gently and thoroughly rub the cream into your skin. 5. Wash your hands with soap and water to remove any residual cream, unless you are treating your hands. 6. You may cover treated areas with normal clothing but avoid using bandages, dressings, or wraps. 7. Be cautious not to wash the cream off treated areas. Avoid swimming, showering, or bathing immediately after application. Consult your doctor about reapplying the cream after these activities. 8. Once the cream is fully absorbed, you may apply moisturizers, sunscreen, or makeup to the treated areas. Ask your doctor about the specific products you plan to use. This medication may be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before using pimecrolimus cream: Inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to pimecrolimus or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Certain medications may interact with pimecrolimus, and your doctor may need to adjust your doses or monitor you for side effects. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had Netherton’s syndrome (a genetic condition causing red, itchy, and scaly skin), widespread redness and peeling of the skin, other skin diseases, or skin infections such as chickenpox, shingles, herpes, or eczema herpeticum. Also, inform your doctor if your eczema rash has become crusty or blistered or if you suspect it is infected. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using pimecrolimus, contact your doctor. Ask your doctor about the safe use of alcohol during treatment, as drinking alcohol may cause your face to flush, turn red, or feel hot. Avoid exposure to chickenpox, shingles, and other viruses. If you are exposed to these viruses while using pimecrolimus, contact your doctor immediately. Good skin care and moisturizers may help alleviate the dryness caused by eczema. Discuss with your doctor which moisturizers to use and always apply them after using pimecrolimus cream. Discuss with your doctor whether you should avoid consuming grapefruit or grapefruit juice while using this medication. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule. Do not apply extra cream to make up for a missed dose. Pimecrolimus may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms and they persist or worsen: Burning, warmth, stinging, soreness, or redness at the application site (contact your doctor if this lasts more than one week) Warts, bumps, or other skin growths Eye irritation Headache Cough Red, stuffy, or runny nose Nosebleed Diarrhea Painful menstrual periods Some side effects may be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience: Sore or red throat Fever Flu-like symptoms Ear pain, discharge, or other signs of infection Hives New or worsening rash Itching Swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs Difficulty breathing or swallowing Crusting, oozing, blistering, or other signs of skin infection Cold sores Chickenpox or other blisters Swollen glands in the neck Pimecrolimus may cause other side effects. Contact your doctor if you experience any unusual problems while using this medication. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store pimecrolimus cream in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
